children: Investors could be underestimating the Bank of Japan's resolve to fight inflation. TS Lombard's Rory Green says in a note that the BoJ "is a poor communicator and markets are equally bad at deciphering the bank's statements." He says it took a while for markets to price a September hike after July's forward guidance. "A similar dynamic is at play now," Green says, as the yen weakens 1% against the dollar even after a new BoJ hike to 1.25%. He acknowledges that political pressure against higher rates supports BoJ doves, but notes the U.S. fights in the opposite direction for a stronger yen. Green expects Japan's monetary tightening to end at 2% by July. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)
